upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex, who's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! You're very welcome – I'm happy to help you with this.

Thanks for letting me know about Alex. To continue assessing your eligibility for Child Benefit for him, I have a few more questions.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Living abroad does affect eligibility, but there are some circumstances where you may still be able to claim Child Benefit.

Could you tell me which country you're currently living in, and are you working as a Crown servant (for example, a diplomat, or working for the armed forces overseas)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not working as a Crown servant, no. I'm just living abroad with my family.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

To help me understand your situation better, could you tell me:

Are you a UK national, and do you have any ongoing connection to the UK – for example, are you paying UK National Insurance contributions, or were you recently living in the UK before moving abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do have a connection to the UK - I'm a UK national and I was living there before I moved abroad. I'm not currently paying National Insurance contributions though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

To continue assessing your eligibility, could you tell me which country you're currently living in? Some countries have social security agreements with the UK that may affect your eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all those specific details right now. Can you just tell me - based on the fact that I'm living abroad and not working for the Crown or paying National Insurance - am I eligible for Child Benefit for Alex or not?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you'd prefer not to go into more detail, and I appreciate your patience.

Based on the information you've provided:

- You are living abroad (not in the UK)
- You are not a Crown servant
- You are not currently paying UK National Insurance contributions

Unfortunately, the general rule for Child Benefit is that you need to **live in the UK** to qualify. There are some exceptions for people who live in certain countries (particularly EEA countries or countries with social security agreements with the UK) or who work as Crown servants abroad, but these exceptions don't appear to apply to your situation based on what you've told me.

Without knowing the specific country you're living in, I cannot say for certain whether any special agreements might apply. However, based on the information provided, it does not appear that you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Would you like me to make a final eligibility decision based on this information, or would you prefer to provide more details about your circumstances?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, that's fine. I understand - since I'm living abroad and don't meet those exceptions, I'm not eligible. Thank you for explaining that to me.
